title: Slice 1 · Task 6 — Runway calculator
description:
Source: docs/slice-1.md → Task 6 — Runway calculator

- [ ] `RunwayCalculator.runway(for site, occupants, lots, products, locations, kits, profiles, on today) -> SiteRunway`.
- [ ] Only lots whose location resolves to this site. Exclude archived lots and lots inside kits with `countsTowardSiteRunway == false`.
- [ ] Food: `low` = kcal from `.good` lots ÷ Σ occupants' kcalPerDay; `high` adds `.caution` and `.inspect`. Expired never counts.
- [ ] Water: same low/high split over potable gallons. Lots tagged non-potable are reported separately as `untreatedNonPotableGal` and not counted (treatment arrives in v1.1).
- [ ] Effective runway = min of food and water, for low and high separately; `limitingCategory` = category that sets the low end.
- [ ] Next target: the first of 3, 14, 30 days above the effective low; report the shortfall for the limiting category in its base unit (kcal or gal).
- [ ] Problems are returned, not thrown: zero occupants → `.noOccupants`; food lots with no kcal data → listed in `lotsMissingNutrition` and excluded.
- [ ] Days are `Double`; no rounding in HearthstockCore.

**Tests:** single-person basics; two people with different kcal targets; caution lots raise only the high end; go-bag excluded by default and included when the flag is on; a lot at another site ignored; zero occupants; missing-kcal lot reported.

**Fixture:** `Fixtures/sample-pantry.json` — one site, two adults (2,400 and 2,000 kcal/day), ~15 realistic lots across a hot garage, a cool-dry closet and a go-bag: e.g. 20 lb white rice (garage), 6 cans black beans with a printed date 14 months ago, a 24-pack of 0.5 L bottled water, 5 gal stored tap water acquired 8 months ago, Mylar-packed beans with no printed date, flour, peanut butter, honey, an MRE in the go-bag. Write the expected food/water low/high values in a comment, computed by hand, and assert them. I'll swap in my real pantry later; the test should keep working with new expected values.

title: Slice 1 · Task 5 — Shelf-life evaluation
description:
Source: docs/slice-1.md → Task 5 — Shelf-life evaluation

- [ ] `ShelfLifeEvaluator.state(of lot, product, profile, climate, on today: CalendarDate) -> LotState` returning `.good`, `.caution`, `.inspect`, `.expired`, plus the computed `usableBy: CalendarDate?`.
- [ ] Rules (spec → Shelf life and Storage climate):
  - `useBy`: good through the printed date, expired after it. No extension, no climate scaling.
  - `bestBy` with printed date: good through printed date; window = extensionMonths × climate multiplier (round down to whole days); caution until the last 20% of the window; inspect for the last 20%; expired after.
  - Packaging `mylarO2`/`bucket` with `packagedLifeMonths`: usable-by = acquired + packagedLifeMonths × climate multiplier. Use whichever of this and the printed-date rule is **later**.
  - No printed date + `rotationMonths`: usable-by = acquired + rotationMonths (no climate scaling); good until the last 20%, then inspect, then expired.
  - `none` with no rotation: always good.
  - No printed date and none of the above: good, and flagged `missingDate` so the UI can nudge later.
  - Refrigerated/frozen climate: out of scope for this slice — evaluate as climateControlled and flag `powerDependent`.
- [ ] Humidity flag: a humid location adds `humidityRisk` to lots whose packaging is `none` (cans, paper, cardboard). It doesn't change dates.

**Tests (table-driven):** each date type; boundary days (exactly on printed date, first caution day, first inspect day, first expired day); hot garage (0.5×) vs cool-dry (1.25×) for the same can; Mylar rice with an old printed date still good; use-by formula one day past → expired; stored tap water at 5 and 7 months.

title: Slice 1 · Task 3 — Domain types
description:
Source: docs/slice-1.md → Task 3 — Domain types

Model these per `docs/spec.md` → Data model. Value types only; include only fields needed in slices 1–2 plus anything the spec marks as v1.

- [ ] `Site`, `Person` (name, kcalPerDay default 2000, waterGalPerDay default 1.0)
- [ ] `Category` (food, water, power, medical, tools, hygiene, other), `ProductRole` (supply, capability, consumable)
- [ ] `Product` (name, barcode?, category, role, baseUnit, kcalPerBaseUnit?, potableWaterGalPerBaseUnit?, shelfLifeProfileKey)
- [ ] `Lot` (product, quantity in base units, acquiredDate, printedDate?, packaging, locationID, climateOverride?, opened, archived)
- [ ] `Location` (siteID, name, parentID?, climateClass?, humidity?, kitID?)
- [ ] `ClimateClass` (coolDry, rootCellar, climateControlled, insulatedUnconditioned, hot, vehicle, refrigerated, frozen) with multipliers from the spec table; `Humidity` (dry, humid); `Packaging` (none, mylarO2, bucket, stabilized)
- [ ] `Kit` (locationID, templateID?, countsTowardSiteRunway — default **false**)
- [ ] Climate resolution: lot override → location → parent chain → `climateControlled` default. Cycles in the parent chain are an error, not an infinite loop.

**Tests:** climate resolution through a 3-level chain, override wins, cycle detected.
close_reason: Domain types + climate resolution with cycle detection; swift test green, 38 tests

title: Slice 1 · Task 2 — Units and quantities
description:
Source: docs/slice-1.md → Task 2 — Units and quantities

- [ ] `UnitKind` with base units: mass → lb, volume → gal, energy → Wh, count → count.
- [ ] Supported entry units: lb, oz, kg, g; gal, qt, L, mL, fl oz; Wh, kWh, mAh@voltage (for battery packs — Wh = mAh × V / 1000); count.
- [ ] `Quantity(value, unit)` with `inBaseUnit()`; converting across kinds is a thrown error, not a crash.

**Tests (table-driven):** 9 kg → 19.84 lb; 24 × 0.5 L → 3.17 gal; 16 fl oz → 0.125 gal; 20,000 mAh @ 3.7 V → 74 Wh; lb → gal throws.
close_reason: Units and Quantity with table-driven tests; swift test green, 24 tests

title: Slice 1 · Task 1 — Calendar dates and IDs
description:
Source: docs/slice-1.md → Task 1 — Calendar dates and IDs

- [ ] `CalendarDate` value type (year, month, day): `Comparable`, `Codable` as ISO `YYYY-MM-DD`, init from ISO string (failable), `adding(months:)` and `adding(days:)` (end-of-month clamping: Jan 31 + 1 month = Feb 28/29), `days(until:)`.
- [ ] Typed IDs for every entity (`SiteID`, `PersonID`, `LocationID`, `ProductID`, `LotID`, `KitID`, `KitTemplateID`).

**Tests:** ISO round-trip, invalid strings rejected, month clamping incl. leap years, day differences across year boundaries.
close_reason: CalendarDate (ISO codable, month clamping, day math) + 7 typed IDs; 17 tests / 77 cases green

title: Slice 1: skeleton + domain core
description:
Source: docs/slice-1.md

**Goal:** a building app skeleton and a fully tested `HearthstockCore` that can take a site's lots and occupants and answer: what state is each lot in, and how many days of food and water does this site have (as a low–high range)?

No persistence, no real UI, no scanning in this slice. Everything here is pure Swift, driven by `swift test`.

Read first: `CLAUDE.md`, and in `docs/spec.md` the sections **Data model**, **Runway dashboard** and **Decisions**.

Start in plan mode: propose the type list, file layout and test plan for tasks 1–6, wait for approval, then work the tasks in order. Commit after each task.

## Out of scope for this slice

GRDB schema and repositories (slice 2), any real UI (slice 3), barcode scanning, Open Food Facts, pantry walk mode, kits-vs-template checking, power, capabilities, cooking fuel, notifications, widgets.

## Definition of done

- `swift test` green; report the test count.
- `xcodegen generate` and the `xcodebuild` build both succeed.
- `HearthstockCore` imports nothing but Foundation.
- Summary lists: files added, public API of `ShelfLifeEvaluator` and `RunwayCalculator`, every assumption you made, and any spec gaps you hit.
